fda.intro: If you already granted Full Disk Access, the permission usually doesn't apply until the app restarts. Try in this order:
fda.step1: Quit the app completely (Task Assistant menu → Quit, or ⌘Q — not just the window) and reopen it.
fda.step2: If it persists: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access. Remove “Task Assistant” from the list with the – button, add it again with + (or toggle the switch off and on), then restart the app.
fda.step3: Make sure there is only one copy of the app (e.g. in Applications) and that the permission is granted to that copy.
fda.title: Can't read iMessage yet.

pipeline.comoFuncionanImportarHistorial: How do “Import history” and “Process new messages” work?
pipeline.enviasteUnMensajeY: Sent a message and it isn't showing? In iMessage, import it first; in WhatsApp it is captured automatically only if that conversation is included in Settings. Then press Process. For the full explanation, see the Help tab.
pipeline.imported: imported {n} new (database now {total}). Press "Process new messages".
pipeline.miraElMotorEn: Watch the engine work: every message it reads, every image/PDF it analyses, and the tasks it proposes.
pipeline.remaining: {n} older messages still queued — press again to continue
pipeline.tomaLosMensajesQue: 2. Process new messages takes the messages that have not been analysed yet and runs them through the AI to propose tasks (they appear in the Inbox). It starts with the most recent, so today's messages are always analysed on the first pass. If you also imported a lot of history, the rest of the queue drains over the following passes, and the status tells you how many older messages are left.
pipeline.traeMensajesViejosA: 1. Import history brings old messages into the app's database. The number you choose is how many per conversation on WhatsApp, and how many in total on iMessage. It only stores the messages — it does not analyse them yet. New messages arriving while the app is open are captured on their own, with no importing needed.

settings.buscarChatPorNombre: Search chat by name or number…
settings.cadaDiaAEsta: Every day at this time the app fetches new messages and proposes tasks automatically. It needs the app to be open (always on, on the Mac Studio).
settings.comoSeVeLa: How the app looks. Automatic follows the appearance set in macOS and changes on its own when that changes.
settings.deQueBaseDe: Which database this instance is reading from and writing to right now — useful if something seems "not to update" (messages or tasks that don't appear).
settings.eligeDeQueConversaciones: Choose which conversations to extract tasks from. No selection = all chats.
settings.espejosDeSoloLectura: Read-only mirrors of your WhatsApp — they never send messages. You can connect several accounts (numbers) at once. To link each one: on that phone open WhatsApp → Settings → Linked devices → Link a device, and scan the QR code.
settings.laIaQueAnaliza: The AI that analyses messages, reads files and answers in Chat. Qwen (Alibaba) and Kimi (Moonshot) work well from China; you can also use DeepSeek, GLM, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible provider.
settings.languageHint: The language of the app and of the assistant's replies. Changing it reloads the app.
settings.modelosPorRolHint: The main model answers in Chat. The cheap one analyses thousands of messages (lower cost). The vision one reads images — on most providers the strongest text model cannot see images at all.
settings.noSelectionAllChats: No selection — all chats are included. Tick some to narrow it down.
settings.notificacionesNativasDeMacos: Native macOS notifications: a morning summary of what's pending, plus nudges that reappear until tasks are done. Make sure the app's notifications are enabled in System Settings → Notifications.
settings.onlyCheckedChats: Only the ticked chats are included.
